ideas.title: The 12-Second Quote That Used To Take 2 Days
ideas.concept: A before/after post breaking down how an N8N + Claude workflow reads inbound enquiries, pulls context from Google Workspace, and drafts a personalised quote in GoHighLevel before the prospect finishes their coffee. Visual: split-screen — left side a messy inbox with 47 unread emails, right side a clean dashboard with a green 'Quote Sent - 12s' timestamp.
ideas.hook: Your competitors are still 'getting back to you next week.' You just closed the deal before lunch.

ideas.title: 73% of Automations Fail For The Same Boring Reason
ideas.concept: A stat/data-driven post exposing why most business owners' automation attempts collapse within 90 days — they automate broken processes instead of fixing them first. Includes a 3-point diagnostic checklist. Visual: a bold red '73%' number over a graveyard of Zapier logos, with Accelod's fix framework underneath.
ideas.hook: Automating a broken process just means you break things faster. Here's the number nobody wants to admit.

ideas.title: How A Roofing Company Fired Its Spreadsheet
ideas.concept: A short case study story about a trades business drowning in job tracking chaos. Alfie rebuilt their ops on GoHighLevel pipelines, Claude-powered job summaries, and N8N syncing everything to Google Sheets for the accountant. Result: 14 hours a week back and zero lost quotes. Visual: a torn spreadsheet printout next to a clean pipeline view on a phone screen.
ideas.hook: They were losing £8k a month in forgotten quotes. The fix wasn't hiring an ops manager.

ig_caption:
He spent 6 months and £4,200 building an automation that broke every Tuesday. 🧨

His setup? Zapier stacked on spreadsheets, glued together with ChatGPT prompts and prayer.

Every Tuesday, a Zap timed out. Leads vanished. Invoices duplicated. His VA spent hours cleaning up the mess.

We rebuilt it in 9 days: N8N running the logic, GoHighLevel handling the CRM, Claude doing the thinking.

Zero breakages in 4 months. He got his Tuesdays back.

Cheap automation isn't cheap. It's the most expensive tax you'll ever pay.

Sound familiar? 👇
